{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZgRw-A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDHaYE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 55, "title": "Complete two standard joystick connectors across core, Wasm and browser", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `8052502b2a41d29dff770b122298e452c9e23dd3`, `Hardware::input` returns `7Fh` whenever PSG R15 bit 6 selects connector two and ignores both joystick common-line outputs. Hardware stores one joystick mask, Wasm exports one setter, and the browser delivers only arrows/Z/X. This prevents independent second-player input on both MSX1 and MSX2. See the [current core](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/blob/8052502b2a41d29dff770b122298e452c9e23dd3/crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs).

## Expected outcome

Provide two independent standard digital joysticks through core, Wasm and ordinary browser keyboard events. Implement connector selection and each connector’s pin-8 common line. Preserve existing connector-one controls and API behavior.

Use one explicit motherboard policy: retain the current fixed R14-input/R15-output peripheral behavior regardless of R7 direction bits, preserving R7 readback and audio controls. Document this compatibility policy rather than claiming universal discrete-AY electrical behavior.

## Context

The [MSX2 Technical Handbook, sections 5.1–5.2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Konamiman/MSX2-Technical-Handbook/master/md/Chapter5a.md) supplies the connector circuit and BIOS interface. R15 bit 6 selects connector 1/2; bits 4/5 drive their respective pin 8. Standard joystick switches connect six inputs to that common line.

Pinned openMSX [MSXPSG.cc](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/sound/MSXPSG.cc) corroborates routing and its default direction override. [MSXJoystick.cc](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/input/MSXJoystick.cc) returns six released inputs when pin 8 is high. These are behavioral references, not new physical measurements. The handbook transcription contains errors; upstream leaves some pin-6/7 feedback behavior uncertain.

Relevant files include `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs`, `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs`, `web/app.js`, usage documentation and native/browser tests. Existing input tests cover connector one and keyboard services. [Existing CI](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/40033054015/job/120685767799) reports 219 Rust and 114 browser passes; those results do not establish the missing behavior. No builds/tests were rerun for this handoff, and no commercial gameplay claim follows.

Keep scope to standard joysticks. Alternate direction wiring, pin-6/7 feedback, mouse/paddle devices, host Gamepad API, Tab delivery and PPI C7 sound remain separate work.

## Pre-merge acceptance

All mandatory implementation, testing and review belong to the Coordinator before merge.

- [ ] Store two independent active-low six-bit input masks, initially released. R14 bits 0–5 report up/down/left/right/trigger A/trigger B from the selected connector when its pin 8 is low; high pin 8 returns `3Fh` for those bits without erasing held state. Preserve R14 bits 6–7 and existing handling of unrelated R15 bits.
- [ ] Add independent register-level expectations for both models, each direction/button, diagonals, simultaneous inputs, selection changes and common-line isolation. With connector masks `2Eh` and `17h`, R15 values `00h`, `40h`, `10h`, `60h`, `20h`, `50h` must produce full R14 values `6Eh`, `57h`, `7Fh`, `7Fh`, `6Eh`, `57h`, respectively. Test the documented fixed-direction policy across all R7 direction-bit combinations without changing sound controls/readback.
- [ ] Preserve `msx_joystick(value)` as connector one and add an indexed two-connector input entry point. Mask host values to six bits; define and test out-of-range connector handling without mutating either input. Release/reset must clear both connectors and keyboard state.
- [ ] Preserve arrows plus Z/X for connector one. Add connector two using I/K/J/L for up/down/left/right and N/M for triggers. Use physical key codes, retain normal keyboard-matrix delivery, and document both mappings. Releasing one key must retain other held inputs on either connector.
- [ ] Add an original cartridge diagnostic executed by the Z80 under bundled, unmodified C-BIOS on both models. Check direct PSG reads plus actual `GTSTCK` and `GTTRIG` calls for both connectors and both triggers, including simultaneous and released states. Assert independent RAM results and visible output; do not substitute host BIOS traps or private BASIC services.
- [ ] Add Playwright coverage using actual keyboard events, compiled Wasm and the diagnostic’s Canvas output at both `/` and `/msx-rust/`. Verify independent simultaneous controls, key-release isolation, focus scoping, Canvas/window blur, visibility loss, Pause/Resume, Reset and model/cartridge transitions without stuck inputs. Include compatibility coverage for the legacy Wasm setter and connector-one controls.
- [ ] Preserve MSX1/MSX2 firmware and keyboard behavior, PSG/SCC audio, disk operation, cartridge SRAM persistence and existing media ownership/provenance safeguards. Fixtures must be original or already lawfully bundled; no proprietary ROM acquisition is required.
- [ ] Run the README checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, with documented browser dependency setup as needed. Record actual results and review the full diff against this Issue under repository review guidance. Resolve blocking findings before merge.

## Optional validation

Compare the original diagnostic’s register/BIOS observations with a pinned openMSX configuration using the same declared direction policy. Physical joystick measurements or lawful two-player software observations may add evidence but are not prerequisites. None was performed for this handoff.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
